title: Cancel Kindle and Audible in 3 Steps

beats.say: You've paid for ten digital audiobooks you never even downloaded.
beats.visual: Extreme close on a black smartphone resting face-down on rain-slick asphalt under a yellow sodium streetlamp.

beats.say: A single forgotten $15 subscription drains $1,800 every ten years. Where's that silent leak actually leading?
beats.visual: Low angle shot looking up at a monolithic corporate glass skyscraper at blue hour, cold fluorescent interior lights cutting through fog.

beats.say: Most people assume deleting the app stops the monthly billing, but Amazon keeps quietly charging your card.
beats.visual: Extreme wide shot of a faceless silhouette sitting inside a parked car at night, viewed through a wet windshield under a buzzing neon light.

beats.say: You can plug this leak in under ten minutes. Step one. Open Amazon in a mobile browser, not the app.
beats.visual: Extreme close-up of hands holding a dark metallic phone, illuminated solely by a single warm practical desk lamp cutting through shadow.

beats.say: Tap your profile icon, scroll down to 'Memberships and Subscriptions', and review every active reading service.
beats.visual: Silhouette of a person standing outside a locked modern glass storefront at blue hour, reflections shimmering on cold wet concrete.

beats.say: Step two. Select Kindle Unlimited, tap 'Cancel Membership', and click through their fake retention discount offer.
beats.visual: Low angle shot of a lone traveler walking through a desolate concrete pedestrian underpass bathed in harsh sodium lighting.

beats.say: That saves you $12 every month. But your Audible account hides an even sneakier financial trap.
beats.visual: Extreme wide shot of massive electrical transmission towers receding into dense fog across an empty dark landscape at dusk.

beats.say: If you cancel Audible immediately, you lose all unspent credits forever. Amazon keeps that cash for free.
beats.visual: Extreme close-up of a blank dark bank card sitting on a scratched steel counter under a solitary downward white spotlight.

beats.say: Step three. Switch your browser to desktop view, spend your banked credits, and then confirm full cancellation.
beats.visual: Silhouette of a person seated on a wet concrete dock edge looking across dark open water toward a quiet container port at night.

beats.say: You'll keep the audiobooks permanently, without paying Amazon another single dime every month.
beats.visual: Low angle shot of a solitary figure standing on a rain-washed bridge overlook, distant vehicle taillights streaking across wet asphalt.

beats.say: Investing an extra $100 a month at 8% compounding grows into $149,036 over 30 years.
beats.visual: Extreme wide cinematic shot of a tiny human figure walking down the center stripe of an empty highway into blue hour dawn.

beats.say: Stop paying monthly fees for books you don't read. Follow for the money rules school never taught you.
beats.visual: High angle shot from the perimeter edge of a brutalist concrete parking tower looking down at empty streets veiled in nocturnal mist.

caption: Deleting the app doesn't cancel the billing. Here's how to kill your forgotten Kindle and Audible subscriptions in under ten minutes.
description: Silent digital subscriptions leak hundreds of dollars every year if you leave them on autopay. Learn the exact 3-step browser sequence to cancel Kindle Unlimited and Audible without forfeiting your credits.
first_comment: How many monthly subscriptions do you currently have running that you haven't opened in 60 days?

facts.basis: Money Fact Sheet: 'A $15/month subscription for 10 years = $1,800'
Money Fact Sheet: '$100/month invested for 30 years at 8%/yr (monthly compounding) = $149,036 (you put in $36,000)'

loop_map.stakes: Leaking $1,800 over a decade on unused digital book subscriptions.
loop_map.big_question: Where's that silent leak actually leading?
loop_map.assume: Deleting reading apps off your phone stops the monthly charges.
loop_map.reveal: Amazon continues billing your credit card until canceled via browser, and Audible cancels unspent credits if you quit early.
